cohort: The cohort consisted of 426 children aged 6-12 years, divided into 213 children diagnosed with Molar-Incisor Hypomineralization (MIH) and 213 healthy controls.
finding: Vaginal delivery and a history of chickenpox were identified as protective factors against Molar-Incisor Hypomineralization (MIH), while preterm birth, frequent analgesic use, and recurrent diarrhea showed modest associations.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was found to be protective against Molar-Incisor Hypomineralization (MIH), reducing the odds by 46%.
